rubrics.rubric: Does the migration guide order breaking changes by customer impact, placing the orderId type fix (DELETE /store/order/{orderId}, 12.3% error rate, 22% migrated) and OAuth 2.0 flow change (POST /pet, 8.7% error rate, 34% migrated) before the PUT /pet 405-to-422 status code change (5.5% error rate, 71% migrated)?
criterion: The migration guide uses quantitative data from api_usage_metrics.json (error rates, affected consumer counts, and migration completion percentages) to determine section ordering of the three breaking changes.

The orderId type fix (DELETE /store/order/{orderId}) appears before the PUT /pet status code change, justified by its 12.3% error rate (10.2 percentage point increase) and only 22% migration completion.
The OAuth 2.0 flow change (POST /pet) appears before the PUT /pet status code change, justified by its 8.7% error rate, 923 affected consumers, and only 34% migration completion.
The PUT /pet 405-to-422 status code change is placed last among the three breaking changes, reflecting its 71% migration completion and decreasing error trend at 5.5% error rate.

rubrics.rubric: Does the migration guide provide before/after code examples in both curl and Python for all 3 breaking changes: (1) OAuth 2.0 implicit-to-authorization-code flow for POST /pet, (2) orderId type change from string to integer (int64) for DELETE /store/order/{orderId}, and (3) status code change from 405 to 422 for PUT /pet validation failures?
criterion: For the OAuth 2.0 change, the guide includes before/after code examples in both curl and Python, where old code shows implicit flow token usage and new code shows authorization code flow with the updated authorization URL /api/oauth/authorize.
For the orderId type change, the guide includes before/after code examples in both curl and Python, where old code passes a string value (e.g., '5A2') and new code passes an integer (int64).

For the PUT /pet status code change, the guide includes before/after code examples in both curl and Python, where old code shows error handling expecting HTTP 405 and new code handles HTTP 422 (Unprocessable Entity).
In the migration guide, all three breaking changes have complete code example pairs in both languages, totaling 6 before/after code example pairs (3 changes × 2 languages).

rubrics.rubric: Does the migration guide include 'Common Migration Pitfalls' subsections drawing from actual support ticket data — specifically referencing SUP-4422 (Enterprise customer's OAuth implicit tokens rejected), SUP-4401 (orderId string '5A2' causing 500 error), and SUP-4438 (Enterprise customer's integration tests breaking due to 405-to-422 change)?
criterion: For the OAuth 2.0 change, the migration guide includes a pitfall subsection referencing SUP-4422, describing how an Enterprise customer's implicit flow tokens were rejected after v3.1.0 with no migration notice.
For the orderId change, the migration guide includes a pitfall subsection referencing SUP-4401, describing how a customer passing '5A2' as orderId got a 500 error instead of 400.

For the PUT /pet change, the migration guide includes a pitfall subsection referencing SUP-4438, describing how an Enterprise customer's integration tests broke because they expected 405 but received 422.
All pitfall subsections in the migration guide are presented as concrete real-world scenarios with specific error details drawn from support ticket data, not abstract or generic warnings.

rubrics.rubric: Does the doc_impact_analysis.csv contain all 10 required columns (issue_source, issue_id, endpoint, description, related_tickets, affected_consumers, error_rate_pct, priority, priority_justification, terminology_violation) and correctly map documentation gaps to corresponding support tickets — including orderId type mismatch to SUP-4401, OAuth 2.0 flow change to SUP-4422, lastLoginDate field to SUP-4491, and quantity validation to SUP-4467?
criterion: The doc_impact_analysis.csv contains all 10 required columns: issue_source, issue_id, endpoint, description, related_tickets, affected_consumers, error_rate_pct, priority, priority_justification, and terminology_violation.

The CSV correctly maps high-error-rate issues to support tickets: orderId type issue → SUP-4401 (affected_consumers=891, error_rate_pct=12.3), OAuth 2.0 flow change → SUP-4422 (affected_consumers=923, error_rate_pct=8.7), and PUT /pet status code change → SUP-4438 (affected_consumers=876, error_rate_pct=5.5).

The CSV correctly maps moderate-impact issues to support tickets: lastLoginDate field → SUP-4491 (affected_consumers=1089, error_rate_pct=3.9), findByTags deprecation → SUP-4472 (affected_consumers=634, error_rate_pct=0.9), and uploadImage format → SUP-4415 (affected_consumers=412, error_rate_pct=6.2).

The CSV correctly maps remaining issues to support tickets: quantity validation → SUP-4467 (affected_consumers=1203, error_rate_pct=4.1), reserved status → SUP-4430, X-Token-Type header → SUP-4451, and rate limit error messaging (R012) → SUP-4480.

rubrics.rubric: Does the doc_impact_analysis.csv assign priority scores (P0-P3) justified by quantitative data — with orderId type change (12.3% error rate, 22% migrated) and OAuth 2.0 flow change (8.7% error rate, 34% migrated) as P0, and lower-impact items like findByTags deprecation (0.9% error rate) as P2 or P3?
criterion: P0 (critical) is assigned to orderId type fix (12.3% error rate, 10.2 percentage point increase, only 22% migrated, Enterprise customer affected per SUP-4401) and OAuth 2.0 flow change (8.7% error rate, 923 consumers, only 34% migrated).

P1 (high) is assigned to PUT /pet 405-to-422 (5.5% error rate, 71% migrated, decreasing trend), uploadImage format issue (6.2% error rate, 412 consumers), and POST /store/order quantity validation (4.1% error rate, 1203 consumers).

P2 (medium) is assigned to lastLoginDate field (3.9% error rate, 1089 consumers), reserved status, and X-Token-Type header; P3 (low) is assigned to findByTags deprecation (0.9% error rate, endpoint still functional).
Each priority_justification entry cites specific quantitative evidence (error rates, consumer counts, or migration percentages) from api_usage_metrics.json to justify the assigned priority score.

rubrics.rubric: Does the migration guide include a client SDK compatibility matrix covering all 3 breaking changes, specifying which SDK versions are affected and which minimum versions support the new behavior?
criterion: The migration guide includes a compatibility matrix in table format covering all 3 breaking changes (OAuth 2.0 flow change, orderId type fix, PUT /pet status code change).
For each breaking change, the matrix indicates which SDK versions will break and which minimum versions support the new behavior.
The matrix includes workarounds for consumers who cannot immediately upgrade their SDK versions.

Since exact SDK version numbers are not provided in reference files, the matrix demonstrates professional judgment with a reasonable structure (e.g., organized by language/SDK with version ranges) rather than omitting this requirement.

rubrics.rubric: Does the revised API reference document the GET /user/login response headers — X-Rate-Limit (integer, int32), X-Expires-After (string, date-time), Set-Cookie, and the new X-Token-Type from v3.0.2 — with data types, descriptions, and example values (addressing R008)?
criterion: The GET /user/login response headers X-Rate-Limit (integer, int32 — calls per hour allowed) and X-Expires-After (string, date-time — UTC date when token expires) are documented with data types, descriptions, and example values.
The Set-Cookie response header for GET /user/login is documented.

The new X-Token-Type response header from v3.0.2 is documented, indicating the token format (Bearer or API-Key), with reference to SUP-4451 where a customer's auth flow intermittently failed due to not handling this header.
All 4 response headers include data types, descriptions, and example values (e.g., X-Rate-Limit: 1000, X-Expires-After: '2025-12-15T12:00:00Z', X-Token-Type: 'Bearer').

rubrics.rubric: Does the migration guide function as a standalone document — including an introduction with v3.1.0 release context, a summary of all 3 breaking changes, the current base URL (https://api.petstore.io/v3), and sufficient context for a developer to use it without the full API reference?
criterion: The migration guide includes an introduction explaining the v3.1.0 release and why migration is urgent.
The guide includes a summary table or list of all 3 breaking changes at the top for quick scanning.

The guide includes the current base URL https://api.petstore.io/v3 (updated from http://petstore.swagger.io/v2 per the v3.0.0 changelog) and sufficient authentication context to understand the OAuth 2.0 flow change.

The guide contains complete before/after code examples and sufficient context that a developer can use it without needing the full API reference; it does not assume familiarity with the full API reference or omit context necessary to understand the breaking changes.
